# `•ucs` — Unicode

`•ucs Y` converts characters to exact integer code points and back, keeping the shape.

```bpl
•ucs "ABC"         ⍝ [65 66 67]ₓ
•ucs 65 66 67      ⍝ "ABC"
```

`E•ucs Y` encodes characters or decodes integer units. `E` is `"UTF-8"`, `"UTF-16"` or `"UTF-32"`.

```bpl
"UTF-8"•ucs 'é'    ⍝ [195 169]ₓ
"UTF-8"•ucs 195 169 ⍝ "é"
```

Encoding forms take vectors; units become singletons.

## Errors

- `DOMAIN`: invalid code point or malformed encoding
